title: Tarakihi catch limits cut to support sustainability
capturedBy: Codex in-app browser, visible official page, excerpt
text:
22 SEPTEMBER 2026
Tarakihi catch limits cut to support sustainability
Lower catch limits for tarakihi stocks will reduce fishing pressure and help promote the recovery of New Zealand’s tarakihi fishery Oceans and Fisheries Minister Shane Jones says.
“I have decided to reduce commercial limits for the combined eastern tarakihi fishery by 20 percent; for the western fishery by around 55 percent; and to set a nationwide recreational daily limit of 10 tarakihi per person,” Mr Jones says.
“These measures will immediately reduce fishing pressure on these tarakihi stocks and put them on more positive trajectories, while allowing a lower level of fishing to continue.
“Around 95 percent of commercially caught tarakihi is sold and consumed in New Zealand. It’s clear that tarakihi is a Kiwi favourite and we all want plenty of them in the water to be enjoyed well into the future.
“My officials will closely monitor the fisheries and review tarakihi stocks again next year. A new scientific stock assessment of east coast tarakihi will be undertaken in 2027, and an updated assessment for the west coast stock is planned for 2028.”
These changes are part of formal reviews undertaken twice-yearly on a range of fish stocks to ensure long-term sustainability and are based on the best available science and information.
This review included proposals for management settings for 22 fish stocks around the country.
More information including the decision letter can be found on MPI’s website
